memory_candidates.content: When a test file (e.g. verify-deploy.sh / run-all.sh / a suite's own standalone invocation) times out under ambient system load, check `uptime` and `ps aux --sort=-%cpu` BEFORE assuming a hang or a regression. An unrelated heavy process tree (e.g. another project's `lake build` spawning 10+ lean/clang jobs) can drive 1-minute load average from ~14 to 48+ on a shared machine, making every forked-subprocess-heavy shell script (doc-lint, gate aggregators) appear to hang when it is actually making real but extremely slow forward progress. Confirm via a short isolated re-run with generous polling (captured PID + kill -0 liveness loop) rather than repeatedly re-issuing the same bounded command with ever-larger timeouts.
